mcqs.q: A record base is defined as:
opts: An interim denture base used to support the record rim material for recording maxillomandibular records
The occluding surfaces fabricated for arranging teeth
The final processed base of the completed denture
A tray used to take the final impression
mcqs.explain: It is also called a denture base; the occluding surfaces built on it are the occlusion rim.

mcqs.q: Record bases are fabricated on the master casts following which appointment?
opts: The 2nd clinical appointment — the final impression appointment
mcqs.explain: They are then used during the 3rd and 4th clinical appointments.

mcqs.q: Record bases are used during the 3rd and 4th clinical appointments for:
opts: Maxillomandibular relation records and arrangement of teeth for the wax trial denture
Border molding and the final impression
mcqs.explain: Border molding and the final impression belong to the 2nd appointment.

mcqs.q: Temporary record bases are characterized by the fact that they:
opts: Are discarded and replaced by denture base material once their role is complete
Become part of the actual base of the finished complete denture
Cannot be used for jaw relation records
mcqs.explain: Their role covers establishing jaw relation, teeth arrangement and try-in.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a PERMANENT record base material?
mcqs.explain: The permanent types are heat-cured acrylic resin and metal (Au, Co-Cr, Ti).

mcqs.q: Which is NOT listed as a type of temporary record base?
mcqs.explain: Metal bases (Au, Co-Cr, Ti) are permanent record bases.

mcqs.q: The metals listed for permanent metallic record bases are:
mcqs.explain: A cast metal base is thin, extremely rigid and dimensionally stable.

mcqs.q: The technique used to build an auto-polymerizing acrylic resin record base is the:
mcqs.explain: Polymer and monomer are added alternately in thin successive layers.

mcqs.q: Undercuts on the master cast are blocked out with modelling wax so that:
opts: The record base can easily be removed from the cast without damaging the master cast
The separating medium is not needed
mcqs.explain: The master cast is the only copy of the patient's anatomy and cannot be replaced without retaking the final impression.

mcqs.q: The separating medium used on the blocked-out master casts forms:
opts: Insoluble calcium alginate, from sodium alginate plus calcium sulfate
A layer of calcium sulfate dihydrate
mcqs.explain: It is applied so the acrylic does not bond to the gypsum of the cast.

mcqs.q: In the sprinkle-on technique, the labial flange is built up by:
opts: Adapting a single sheet of dough
Painting on a mixed slurry in one application
mcqs.explain: Building in thin successive layers is how an even, void-free base is obtained.

mcqs.q: Over the palate, the instruction is to:
opts: Sprinkle on a thin consistent layer
Adapt a sheet of baseplate wax
mcqs.explain: The finished palate should be a consistent 2 mm thick and well adapted.

mcqs.q: The ridge crest is reinforced during construction in order to:
opts: Reduce the amount of monomer needed
mcqs.explain: While the resin is soft it flows downhill under its own weight, and the crest is the region that will carry the rim and the teeth.

mcqs.q: The surface is kept moist with monomer during the sprinkle-on technique in order to:
mcqs.explain: A dry sprinkle leaves unwetted polymer beads that become voids in the finished base.

mcqs.q: The cast is manipulated (turned and tilted) during construction in order to:
opts: Prevent slumping while the flanges are built up
Mix the polymer and monomer more thoroughly
mcqs.explain: Gravity is used to keep the soft resin over the area being built.

mcqs.q: Which portion of the base is specifically reinforced along with the ridge crest?
opts: The lingual portion of the flange
The labial portion of the flange
mcqs.explain: In the mandible the lingual flange is the thinnest and most exposed part of the base.

mcqs.q: The pressure used to process the record base in a pressure pot is:
mcqs.explain: Pressure keeps dissolved gas in solution while the resin cures, giving a dense, non-porous base.

mcqs.q: The water temperature and time for processing the record base in a pressure pot are:
mcqs.explain: In the absence of a pressure pot the casts are placed under an over-turned rubber mixing bowl.

mcqs.q: If a pressure pot is not available, the casts are:
opts: Placed under an over-turned rubber mixing bowl
Left in open air with a fan
mcqs.explain: The over-turned bowl traps monomer vapour so the surface does not dry out.

mcqs.q: Before prying the record base off, the base and cast are soaked in hot water to:
mcqs.explain: The base is then gently pried from the master cast.

mcqs.q: The two areas requiring modification on an unfinished record base are the:
opts: Ridge crest and the retromolar pad
mcqs.explain: Flash is the thin excess acrylic extending beyond the intended border.

mcqs.q: According to the checklist, the palate of a completed record base should be:
opts: A consistent 2 mm thick and well adapted to the tissue surface
As thin as possible, about 0.5 mm
Variable in thickness to allow flexing
mcqs.explain: Thick enough to be rigid, thin enough not to crowd the tongue or distort speech at the try-in.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT part of the completed record base checklist?
opts: No excess flash on the land area of the master casts
mcqs.explain: The checklist calls for a well-adapted tissue surface with no porosity or voids, roughened ridge areas, thin areas labial to the ridge, and smooth rounded flanges.

mcqs.q: The ridge areas of the record base are deliberately roughened in order to:
opts: Give the wax occlusion rim something to grip
Reduce the weight of the base
Improve the appearance of the base
mcqs.explain: The rim must not peel off the base while jaw records are being taken.

mcqs.q: An occlusion rim is defined as:
opts: Occluding surfaces fabricated on record bases for the purpose of making maxillomandibular relation records and arranging teeth
An interim denture base supporting the record rim material
The wax used to block out undercuts on the master cast
The flat plate used to form the occlusal plane
mcqs.explain: It is also called a record rim.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT one of the stated uses of record bases and occlusion rims?
opts: Recording the border extension of the denture
Establishing and maintaining the vertical dimension of occlusion
A waxed-up mold for the external surface of the complete denture
mcqs.explain: The six uses are facial contours, tooth selection, vertical dimension of occlusion, interocclusal records, teeth arrangement, and the waxed-up mold; border extension is recorded at border molding.

mcqs.q: The material used for making occlusion rims is:
mcqs.explain: It is supplied as sheets that are softened and rolled, and also as ready-made horseshoe-shaped blanks.

mcqs.q: The landmarks marked on the master casts before building the rims are:
opts: The midline, the crest of the ridge, and the midpoint of the retromolar pad
The hamular notch, the fovea palatinae and the incisive papilla
The depth of the vestibule all round
mcqs.explain: These landmarks will be used to check teeth arrangement.

mcqs.q: The instruments and materials listed for making occlusion rims are:
opts: Baseplate wax, wax knife & scale, occlusal plane former (hot plate), and master casts with denture bases
Acrylic burs, straight handpiece, polymer and monomer
Pressure pot, rubber bowl and separating medium
Beading wax, boxing wax and dental stone
mcqs.explain: The occlusal plane former is a flat heated blade or plate used to flatten the occlusal surface.

mcqs.q: The height of the maxillary occlusion rim from the labial frenum is:
mcqs.explain: 12 mm is its height in the tuberosity, measured from the record base.

mcqs.q: The height of the maxillary occlusion rim in the tuberosity, measured from the record base, is:
mcqs.explain: The rim is taller in front and shorter behind, and that difference creates the occlusal plane.

mcqs.q: The height of the mandibular occlusion rim from the labial frenum is:
mcqs.explain: Posteriorly it reaches the mid-point or two-thirds of the retromolar pad.

mcqs.q: Posteriorly, the mandibular occlusion rim is built to:
opts: The mid-point or two-thirds of the retromolar pad
The full height of the retromolar pad
The level of the hamular notch
mcqs.explain: The retromolar pad is one of the few landmarks that does not resorb, so its height is a reliable guide to the original occlusal plane.

mcqs.q: The width of the occlusion rim posteriorly and anteriorly is:
mcqs.explain: These widths are the same for the maxillary and the mandibular rim.

mcqs.q: In the procedure for making the maxillary rim, the roll of wax is first pressed against the crest of the ridge starting at the:
mcqs.explain: The wax is then sealed to the record base with a wax knife.

mcqs.q: The occlusal aspect of the rim is formed by:
opts: Heating the occlusal plane former in a flame and carefully forming the occlusal surface
Carving it freehand with a wax knife only
Pressing it against the opposing cast
Trimming it with an acrylic bur
mcqs.explain: The buccal and labial contours are then formed with the wax knife.

mcqs.q: According to the maxillary wax rim checklist, the curvature of the anterior portion must:
opts: Simulate the curvature of the edentulous arch
Be a straight line across the arch
Follow the curve of the palatal vault
Be flat to allow the teeth to be set
mcqs.explain: The labial and palatal surfaces must also be smooth and free of voids.

mcqs.q: Compared with the maxillary rim, the mandibular rim is fabricated in a similar manner except that it:
opts: Should be centered over the crest of the ridge
Should be placed buccal to the crest of the ridge
Should be placed lingual to the crest of the ridge
mcqs.explain: A rim off the crest loads the ridge eccentrically and the base tips on closure, giving a wrong jaw record.

mcqs.q: The lingual contours of the mandibular occlusion rim must be:
opts: Concave and must not impinge on the tongue space
mcqs.explain: The rim is also centred over the ridge to maximize stability.

mcqs.q: The face-bow is used at the jaw relation appointment to record the:
opts: Orientation relation of the maxilla to the hinge axis
mcqs.explain: It allows the casts to be mounted on the articulator in the same spatial position they occupy in the patient's skull.

saqs.q: Define a record base and list the materials used to make record bases.
saqs.a: A record base is an interim denture base used to support the record rim material for recording maxillomandibular records; it is also called a denture base. The materials fall into two groups. Temporary record bases are discarded and replaced by denture base material once their role in establishing jaw relation, teeth arrangement and try-in is complete; their types are the shellac base plate, the reinforced shellac base plate, chemically cured acrylic resin, and visible light cured (VLC) acrylic resin. Permanent record bases are not discarded and become part of the actual base of the finished complete denture; their types are heat cured acrylic resin and metal (gold, cobalt-chromium, titanium).

saqs.q: Describe the preparation of the master cast before an auto-polymerizing record base is built on it.
saqs.a: Two preparatory steps are required. First, block out the undercuts with modelling wax, so that the record base can easily be removed from the cast without damaging the master cast. Second, apply the separating medium: sodium alginate plus calcium sulfate gives insoluble calcium alginate, and the blocked out master casts are coated with this separating media so that the acrylic resin does not stick to the cast.

saqs.q: Describe the sprinkle-on technique for constructing an auto-polymerizing acrylic resin record base.
saqs.a: The maxillary record base is built directly on the prepared master cast by alternating additions of polymer and monomer. Build up the labial flange by alternating polymer and monomer addition. Sprinkle on a thin consistent layer over the palate. Reinforce the ridge crest to prevent slumping. Keep the surface moist with monomer to prevent porosity. Manipulate the cast to prevent slumping and build up the flanges. Reinforce the lingual portion of the flange and the ridge crest. The base is then polymerized, removed, and trimmed.

saqs.q: Describe the polymerization and removal of the record base, and list the areas requiring modification.
saqs.a: Process the acrylic resin in a pressure pot at 20 psi pressure, in 45 degrees C water, for 10 to 15 minutes. In the absence of a pressure pot, place the casts under an over-turned rubber mixing bowl. To remove the base, soak the polymerized record base and casts in hot water to soften the block-out wax, then gently pry the record bases from the master cast. The areas requiring modification on an unfinished record base are the land, where resin has run out onto the land area of the master cast, and the flash, which is the thin excess acrylic beyond the intended border; the excess acrylic or flash is trimmed away and the flanges are smoothed and rounded.

saqs.q: Give the checklist for a completed record base.
saqs.a: The palate should be a consistent 2 mm thick and well adapted to the tissue surface. The ridge areas should be roughened. There should be thin areas labial to the ridge. The retromolar pad area should be covered. There should be no porosity or voids on the tissue surface. The flanges should be smooth and rounded. The tissue surface should be well adapted. And there should be no excess flash (acrylic) on the land area of the master casts.

saqs.q: Define an occlusion rim, list its uses, and give the dimensions of the maxillary and mandibular rims.
saqs.a: An occlusion rim is the occluding surfaces fabricated on record bases for the purpose of making maxillomandibular relation records and arranging teeth; it is also called a record rim. The record base and occlusion rims are necessary for (1) establishing facial contours, (2) help in tooth selection, (3) establishing and maintaining the vertical dimension of occlusion, (4) making interocclusal records, (5) the arrangement of the denture teeth, and (6) a waxed-up mold for the external surface of the complete denture. The maxillary occlusion rim is 22 mm in height from the labial frenum, 12 mm in height in the tuberosity from the record base, 8 to 10 mm wide posteriorly and 6 to 8 mm wide anteriorly. The mandibular occlusion rim is 18 mm in height from the labial frenum, reaching the mid-point or two-thirds of the retromolar pad posteriorly, and is likewise 8 to 10 mm wide posteriorly and 6 to 8 mm wide anteriorly.

saqs.q: Explain the technique of making an occlusion rim and give the checklist for the finished rim.
saqs.a: The instruments and materials are baseplate wax, a wax knife and scale, an occlusal plane former (hot plate), and the master casts with denture bases; the casts are first marked to indicate the midline, the crest of the ridge and the midpoint of the retromolar pad, and these landmarks are used to check teeth arrangement. The procedure is: (a) place the maxillary record base on the cast; (b) heat a sheet of baseplate wax in the Bunsen burner until the wax is soft; (c) roll the wax into a long tube; (d) starting at the tuberosity, press the roll of wax against the crest of the ridge; (e) seal the wax to the record base with a wax knife; (f) heat the occlusal plane former in a flame and carefully form the occlusal aspect of the rim; and (g) form the buccal and labial contours with the wax knife. For the maxillary rim the occlusal portion should be 8 to 10 mm thick in the posterior region and 6 to 8 mm in the anterior region, the labial and palatal surfaces must be smooth and free of voids, and the curvature of the anterior portion must simulate the curvature of the edentulous arch. The mandibular wax rim is fabricated in a similar manner, but the rim should be centered over the crest of the ridge to maximize stability, its lingual contours must be concave and must not impinge on the tongue space, and posteriorly it intersects one half to two thirds up the retromolar pad.
